title: Collector pruning policy and sample-proof guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This is a working draft to capture a lightweight, enforceable collector pruning policy and a set of guidance notes for producing verifiable samples ("proofs") sent to downstream SIEM/export pipelines. Goal is to reduce long-term storage cost, improve auditability of retained evidence, and make retention decisions deterministic for compliance review.

Audience:
- Security & compliance engineers
- SREs operating collectors
- Platform engineers integrating RBAC v2 with collectors
- Product owners who need evidence retention SLAs

High-level goals:
- Define clear TTLs and pruning triggers for ephemeral vs canonical evidence.
- Define sampling strategy with cryptographic proof metadata so sampled items are provable subsets of full ingest.
- Ensure RBAC v2 enforcement points for evidence read/export are defined and auditable.
- Map audit events (collector lifecycle + prune + sample) to SIEM export schema.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not prescribe exact storage tiers (S3 classes) or infra billing allocation.
- Not a full legal retention schedule. This is engineering policy with hooks for legal to consume.

Definitions (informal):
- Raw capture: original event payload produced by source (application, infra) prior to normalization.
- Canonical evidence: normalized, indexed event we keep long-term (e.g., hashed, PII-normalized).
- Ephemeral buffer: short-lived store for buffering and batching (minutes -> hours).
- Proof bundle: metadata package that proves a sampled canonical evidence item was part of an original ingestion set.

Policy outline:
1) Classify evidence at ingest time into three classes: ephemeral, canonical-short, canonical-long.
   - ephemeral: TTL = 24 hours; reason: high-volume, low-audit-value (debug traces).
   - canonical-short: TTL = 90 days; reason: operational investigations and short legal holds.
   - canonical-long: TTL = 7 years (or per contract); reason: compliance-bound artifacts.
   - Default class assigned by capture rules and route policies; team can override by tag.

2) Pruning triggers and safe-deletion flow:
   - Soft-delete: mark objects for deletion and move to "pending-prune" for 7 days. During this window, evidence can be restored by oncall or automated retention-extension.
   - Hard-delete: after pending-prune window expires, objects are removed from primary indexes and archived with hashed-summary if in ephemeral class.
   - Canonical-long items never hard-delete without documented legal/retention workflow.

3) Sampling strategy and proofs:
   - Sampling occurs when retention-cost > threshold OR when sample set is required for periodic audits.
   - Deterministic sampling algorithm: hash(source_id || ingestion_epoch || shared-salt) % N -> decide sample. Salt rotation policy is tracked in KMS and audited.
   - Proof bundle contents (minimal): sample_algorithm, salt_version, source_id, ingestion_epoch, canonical_id, sha256(original_payload) (or canonical digest), signature(kms_key_id, signature).
   - Proof bundles are small JSON documents attached to exported sample rows and stored for retention period equal to sampled item TTL or audit TTL, whichever longer.

4) RBAC v2 enforcement points:
   - Read/export endpoint must check: principal -> role -> allowed_evidence_classes (ephemeral/canonical-short/canonical-long) -> allowed_exports (SIEM, SFTP, console).
   - Collector agents that perform pruning need a "pruner" service account with constrained scope (can mark pending-prune, can soft-delete metadata). Hard-delete privilege requires a separate role and two-person approval for canonical-long.
   - Mapping notes: use centralized policy engine (opa / rbac-v2 adapter) with cache TTL of 1 minute; audit every decision to audit-log with context.

Audit log schema (evidence lifecycle events):
- Minimal required fields for each audit event (CSV-friendly header):
  event_id, event_type, timestamp, actor, actor_id, actor_role, resource_type, resource_id, resource_class, action, result, reason, prev_ttl, new_ttl, sample_algorithm, salt_version, signature_ref, request_id

- Example event lines (human-readable):
  event_type: "sample-selected"
  actor: "collector-01"
  actor_role: "collector-service"
  resource_id: "canonical-ev-2025-11-12-0a1b"
  resource_class: "canonical-short"
  action: "mark_sampled"
  sample_algorithm: "mod-hash-v1"
  signature_ref: "kms://projects/rw/keys/evidence-sig/v3/2025-11-12"

- Encryption/PII guidance: audit payloads must never include raw PII values. If proof requires PII, store a one-way tokenized id and reference to a secure vault that holds decryption audit-trail.

SIEM export mapping notes (Elastic/CEF-friendly):
- Prefer ECS-compatible fields where feasible. Minimal export mapping:
  @timestamp -> timestamp
  event.dataset -> evidence.lifecycle
  event.kind -> event_type
  agent.name -> actor
  user.name -> actor_id (if user-driven)
  process.name -> collector_agent
  file.hash.sha256 -> resource_digest
  cloud.account.id -> project_id
  tags -> [sample, pruned, canonical-long]
  tags.release -> retention-policy

- Export transport options: HTTPS with mTLS to SIEM forwarder, or batched S3 export with manifest (manifest contains sha256 of batch and pointer to proof bundles). Batched export must include manifest signed by platform KMS and a coordination id for replay.

Operational runbook (high-level steps):
- Nightly prune job: evaluate TTLs, mark pending-prune, emit audit events to evidence.audit_stream.
- Weekly sample job: run deterministic sampler for targets configured by compliance, persist proof bundles, and export sample manifest to SIEM.
- Emergency retention-extend: oncall CLI allows retention-extension for an object with justification recorded and an audit event emitted. Requires approver id for canonical-long.

Observability & alerting:
- Metrics to emit: items_marked_pending, items_hard_deleted, sample_rate_by_source, sample_proof_creation_errors, prune_job_latency, prune_job_failures, retention-extend-count.
- Tracing: requests should carry trace_id from source -> collector -> pruner -> export. Record trace_id in audit events.

Open questions / trade-offs (notes-to-self):
- How often should salt be rotated? Monthly rotation reduces replay risk but complicates deterministic sampling across month boundaries. Propose rotate quarterly and record salt_version in proofs.
- Performance impact of attaching full sha256 of original payload for every sample proof in very-high-volume sources. Could store canonical digest only; if legal asks for raw, run on-demand fetch from short-term buffer with audit gating.
- Two-person approval UX for hard-delete of canonical-long: Slack + web UI vs ticketed flow.

Implementation to-dos (practical):
- [ ] Add sample_algorithm module to collector open-source repo (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/evidence-collector/pull/88).
- [ ] Add RBAC v2 policy templates for pruner/read/export roles (Confluence ID in linked_artifacts).
- [ ] Wire audit event producer to central evidence.audit_stream (team: observability).
- [ ] Create SIEM manifest schema and sign/verify tool for batched exports.

Appendix A: Quick example proof bundle (single-line JSON blob, shown pretty for clarity):
  {
    "proof_id": "proof-20251112-0a1b",
    "canonical_id": "canonical-ev-2025-11-12-0a1b",
    "source_id": "svc-order-42",
    "ingestion_epoch": "2025-11-12T17:23:01Z",
    "sample_algorithm": "mod-hash-v1",
    "salt_version": "v3",
    "digest": "sha256:3f2a...",
    "signature_ref": "kms://projects/rw/keys/evidence-sig/v3/2025-11-12",
    "stored_location": "s3://evidence-proofs/2025/11/12/proof-20251112-0a1b.json"
  }

Appendix B: Suggested alerts and SLIs:
- SLI: proof_bundle_success_rate >= 99.9% per 24h window.
- SLI: nightly_prune_jobs_complete < 30m.
- Alert: prune_job_failures > 0 for 5m (pager to eng-sre).

Notes: This doc is intentionally pragmatic and engineering-facing; expect iteration after an initial pilot with two collectors (order-service and auth-service) and one SIEM integration.

Scratchpad / conversation snippets:
- "If salt rotates quarterly, we can still do cross-quarter audits by keeping salt history for 3 quarters." — Sophie
